title: Curated picks per traveler type (ATIA AI Take-Home Kit, tool 1.b)
description: The JSON block the 1.b run prompt asks the AI for: one object per traveler type, each with up to three picks from the operator's inventory. Each product_id refers to a row of the inventory (inventory-template.csv). Each cited_fact is copied word for word from that row. The checker at preig.github.io/atiakit/1b/ also tests what a schema cannot: that product_id exists in the inventory, that cited_fact appears in that row, and that no number appears that the inventory does not contain. Output from an AI is a DRAFT - PENDING OWNER REVIEW until each business approves its own lines.

traveler_type.description: Copied exactly from the operator's list of traveler types, for example "Family with children under 10".

picks.description: Up to three trips, strongest first. Fewer is fine; padding is not.

note_if_fewer_than_three.description: Why fewer than three trips fit, in plain words. Empty string when there are three picks.

product_id.description: The product_id of a row in the inventory, for example "BL-CRUISE-4H".

business.description: The business named in that row.

reason.description: One or two sentences a traveler could check. No prices, availability, discounts, reviews, ratings, awards or superlatives.

cited_fact.description: One fact copied word for word from that row, optionally starting with the column name, for example "Minimum age 4" or "15 minutes by car from the harbor".

picks.reason: Children aged 2 and up can ride, and the ride takes 90 minutes. It runs in rain, so a wet day does not cancel the plan.

examples.note_if_fewer_than_three: Fictional example, shortened to one pick.
